14 · Spatial E/I arrangement at fixed fraction and strengths¶

Goal¶

Compare source placement on the established FHN synaptic lattice while fixing graph, source counts, conductance protocol, intrinsic dynamics and matched initial conditions. Study a compact inhibitory patch, a broad band, alternating stripes, a checkerboard, and two random assignments.

This notebook and results/fhn_ei_spatial_arrangement/ are separate from notebook 13 and its outputs, so both may be run independently. All necessary code is embedded; no previous notebook execution, downloaded data or internet connection is required. Requires NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib and Jupyter. All variables and time are dimensionless; no physiological calibration or universal placement optimum is inferred.

Observed results¶

24 experiments completed; all 25 structural/numerical checks pass; six figures are saved. Source counts, intrinsic equations and conductances are fixed across layouts within each ratio cut. At ratio 1, all layouts use exactly the same G=0.02A matrix; only outgoing reversal placement differs.

The following results use ratio 1 and time 400–1000. R is event phase order and C is the local uncancelled input fraction, both defined below:

Layout Cross-type edges / 72 Global R, seed 11 Global R, seed 29 C, seed 11
patch 18 0.487 0.183 0.585
band 12 0.196 0.185 0.683
stripes 36 0.099 0.172 0.392
checker 72 0.660 0.766 1.000
random_301 42 0.280 0.496 0.505
random_302 40 0.251 0.263 0.509

Spatial arrangement changes the measured dynamics in these examples, but initial-phase sensitivity is substantial: the patch has R≈0.487 versus 0.183 across the two initial fields. Two fields do not establish a robust ranking or a universal relation between contact counts and synchronization. Checkerboard C=1 follows from geometry: each recipient receives only the opposite source type, so local E/I cancellation is absent despite equal global E/I counts.

The longer-window audit remains important. For ratio 1, seed 11, checkerboard R rises from 0.6603 in time 400–1000 to 0.8424 in time 1400–2000; patch R changes from 0.4867 to 0.4449 and random_301 from 0.2797 to 0.2216. These results retain continuing transients/window dependence rather than asserting settled attractors. Snapshot appearances and low global R do not establish wave type, disorder or chaos.

For the selected random_301 trajectory, independent solvers agree within 3.17e-09 in state over 0–200, while tighter DOP853 agrees within 4.06e-08 over 0–1000. Translation equivariance and source-count/mean-budget identities also pass. These accuracy audits have the stated scope and do not certify every possible parameter or layout.

Setup: isolate arrangement within each strength cut¶

Keep the 6×6 periodic four-neighbor graph, no self-loops, spacing 1, and the preceding equations: $$\dot v_i=v_i-v_i^3/3-w_i+0.5+\sum_jG_{ij}s_j(E_j-v_i),\quad \dot w_i=0.08(v_i+0.7-0.8w_i),$$ $$\dot s_j=\mathrm{sigmoid}(v_j/0.1)(1-s_j)-0.2s_j,\qquad E_E=3,\ E_I=-3.$$ Rows receive from source columns. Every layout has 18 E and 18 I sources and identical FHN dynamics; E/I labels specify outgoing synapses. Gates start at zero and use graded release, not spike-triggered jumps.

For each of two ratios ρ=gI/gE (1 and 2), use the fixed-mean protocol from notebook 13: $$g_E=0.02/(0.5+0.5\rho),\quad g_I=\rho g_E,\quad G_{ij}=A_{ij}g_{type(j)}.$$ The network-average coefficient sum is 0.08 for every case. Within a ratio cut, the E/I strengths are identical across layouts. At ρ=1, G=0.02A is exactly the same matrix for every layout: source reversal placement alone differs. At ρ=2, rearranging source types also redistributes recipient coefficient totals through neighbor composition, while preserving the network mean. This is an explicit mechanism of arrangement, not a claim of identical local budgets or currents.

Six layouts × two ratios × two phase seeds (11/29) = 24 runs. Phase seeds sample an isolated cycle; the same full initial state is reused across every layout/ratio for a given seed. End time 1000; measure 400–1000, step 0.5. Random layouts use assignment seeds 301/302, independently of initial-phase seeds. These are two specific random realizations, not a random-layout ensemble estimate.

def adjacency(side):
 if side<3:raise ValueError('Use side >=3')
 A=np.zeros((side**2,side**2))
 for r in range(side):
  for c in range(side):

 return A

1. Specify the geometry rather than assigning informal labels¶

All coordinates are zero-based. The inhibitory patch contains rows 1–4/columns 1–4 (16 nodes), plus (0,2),(0,3). It is a declared compact shape, not an optimized cluster. The inhibitory band occupies columns 0–2; stripes occupy odd columns; the inhibitory checkerboard occupies odd row+column parity. The torus wraps opposite boundaries, so a band has two interfaces rather than the edge behavior of an open box. The random masks have exactly 18 I sources each.

Within-type components use only same-type nearest-neighbor edges, with isolated nodes counted as components. They are graph descriptors, not neuronal attractors. For a uniformly random half/half source assignment, expected same-type fraction at any distinct edge is 17/35; a realized random mask need not attain that value. This finite-count reference follows by sampling endpoints without replacement.

Translations or rotations of a layout are not automatically independent geometries on an isotropic periodic lattice. Simultaneously transforming graph labels, source types and initial states must preserve dynamics. A translation-equivariance check below tests that indexing contract; holding the random initial field fixed while moving only source labels is a different experiment.

2. Integrate identical dynamics from matched initial fields¶

Use the full synaptic FHN ODE and adaptive event interpolation, without phase reduction or sequential node updates. Preserve the preceding tight solver tolerances. The isolated-cycle construction and complete node initial states are saved. Only three selected trajectories are retained in memory; the other runs are measured and released. All metrics and spike events are saved for every run.

In [3]:
def inputs(v,s,G,E):return G@(s*E)-v*(G@s)
def rhs_values(y,currents,G,E):
 v,w,s=y.reshape(-1,3).T
 return np.column_stack((v-v**3/3-w+currents+inputs(v,s,G,E),EPS*(v+A_REC-B_REC*w),
  ALPHA*expit(v/WIDTH)*(1-s)-BETA*s)).ravel()
def jacobian(y,G,E):
 n=len(E);v,w,s=y.reshape(n,3).T;q=expit(v/WIDTH);J=lil_matrix((3*n,3*n))
 degree=G@s
 for i in range(n):
  J[3*i,3*i]=1-v[i]**2-degree[i];J[3*i,3*i+1]=-1
  J[3*i+1,3*i]=EPS;J[3*i+1,3*i+1]=-EPS*B_REC
  J[3*i+2,3*i]=ALPHA*q[i]*(1-q[i])*(1-s[i])/WIDTH
  J[3*i+2,3*i+2]=-ALPHA*q[i]-BETA
  for j in G.getrow(i).indices:J[3*i,3*j+2]=G[i,j]*(E[j]-v[i])
 return J.tocsr()
def integrate(initial,G,E,end=END,method='DOP853',rtol=1e-10,atol=1e-12):
 initial=np.asarray(initial,float);G=np.asarray(G,float);E=np.asarray(E,float);n=len(E)
 if initial.shape!=(n,3) or G.shape!=(n,n):raise ValueError('Shape mismatch')
 if not np.isfinite(initial).all() or not np.isfinite(G).all() or not np.isfinite(E).all() or np.any(G<0) or np.any(np.diag(G)!=0):raise ValueError('Invalid state or conductance')
 if np.any(initial[:,2]<0) or np.any(initial[:,2]>1):raise ValueError('Initial gate outside [0,1]')
 Gs=csr_matrix(G);events=[]
 for i in range(n):
  def event(t,y,index=i):return y[3*index]
  event.direction=1;event.terminal=False;events.append(event)
 options={}
 if method in ['Radau','BDF']:options['jac']=lambda t,y:jacobian(y,Gs,E)
 sol=solve_ivp(lambda t,y:rhs_values(y,.5,Gs,E),(0,end),initial.ravel(),method=method,
  rtol=rtol,atol=atol,events=events,dense_output=True,max_step=.25,**options)
 if not sol.success:raise RuntimeError(sol.message)
 return sol
iso=integrate([[2.,-.5,0.]],np.zeros((1,1)),np.array([3.]),end=800.,rtol=1e-10,atol=1e-12)
t0,t1=iso.t_events[0][-2:];PERIOD=t1-t0
INITIAL={};init_rows=[]
for seed in PHASE_SEEDS:
 phases=np.random.default_rng(seed).uniform(0,1,N)
 states=iso.sol(t0+phases*PERIOD).reshape(3,N).T;states[:,2]=0;INITIAL[seed]=states
 for node,(q,z) in enumerate(zip(phases,states)):init_rows.append(dict(phase_seed=seed,node=node,phase_fraction=q,v=z[0],w=z[1],s=z[2]))
pd.DataFrame(init_rows).to_csv(OUT/'initial_states.csv',index=False)
print('Reference isolated period:',PERIOD)

3. Measure phase populations, activity and input cancellation¶

Keep global centered v,w RMS spread, node count/period frequencies and ISI variability, source-population and geometric parity phase order, and $$C=\langle|J_i^E+J_i^I|\rangle_{i,t}/\langle|J_i^E|+|J_i^I|\rangle_{i,t}.$$ C is the local uncancelled fraction, not a full definition of dynamic E/I balance. Event phases interpolate only between observed positive v=0 crossings; each order parameter uses times bracketed by events for every node in its group. Valid-time fractions are saved, unsupported phases stay missing, and source groups have equal size here. Low global order is not by itself evidence of disorder or chaos.

Count-frequency resolution is 1/600 per node; period frequency and ISI CV require three retained events. A zero count would be a finite-window observation rather than proof of stable rest. Means use the stated time sampling. Individual phase realizations are shown; two realizations do not justify confidence intervals, significance tests or full basin claims.

def phase_order(phase,mask):
 if not np.any(mask):return np.nan,0.
 valid=np.isfinite(phase[mask]).all(axis=0)
 if not valid.any():return np.nan,0.
 return float(np.abs(np.mean(np.exp(1j*phase[mask][:,valid]),axis=0)).mean()),float(valid.mean())
def measure(sol,mask,G,start=BURN,stop=END):
 times=np.arange(start,stop+DT/10,DT);z=sol.sol(times).reshape(N,3,-1);v,w,s=z[:,0],z[:,1],z[:,2]
 G=csr_matrix(G);E=np.where(mask,3.,-3.)
 JE=inputs(v,s*mask[:,None],G,E[:,None]);JI=inputs(v,s*(~mask)[:,None],G,E[:,None])
 phase=np.full((N,len(times)),np.nan);node_rows=[]
 for i,e in enumerate(sol.t_events):
  recent=e[(e>=start)&(e<=stop)];isi=np.diff(recent)
  if len(e)>=2:
   valid=(times>=e[0])&(times<=e[-1]);phase[i,valid]=np.interp(times[valid],e,2*np.pi*np.arange(len(e)))
  node_rows.append(dict(node=i,source_type='E' if mask[i] else 'I',window_spikes=len(recent),count_frequency=len(recent)/(stop-start),
   period_frequency=float(1/isi.mean()) if len(isi)>=2 else np.nan,isi_cv=float(isi.std()/isi.mean()) if len(isi)>=2 else np.nan,
   mean_E_input=float(JE[i].mean()),mean_I_input=float(JI[i].mean()),rms_E_input=float(np.sqrt(np.mean(JE[i]**2))),rms_I_input=float(np.sqrt(np.mean(JI[i]**2)))))
 nodes=pd.DataFrame(node_rows);centered=z[:,:2]-z[:,:2].mean(axis=0,keepdims=True)
 total=float(np.mean(abs(JE)+abs(JI)));C=float(np.mean(abs(JE+JI))/total) if total>1e-15 else np.nan
 row=dict(state_spread=float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.sum(centered**2,axis=1)))),mean_count_frequency=float(nodes.count_frequency.mean()),
  std_count_frequency=float(nodes.count_frequency.std(ddof=0)),nodes_with_spikes=int((nodes.window_spikes>0).sum()),
  mean_E_input=float(JE.mean()),mean_I_input=float(JI.mean()),local_uncancelled_fraction=C,
  E_count=int(mask.sum()),I_count=int((~mask).sum()))
 for name,pop in [('all',np.ones(N,dtype=bool)),('E',mask),('I',~mask),('even',PARITY),('odd',~PARITY)]:
  order,coverage=phase_order(phase,pop);row[f'phase_order_{name}']=order;row[f'phase_coverage_{name}']=coverage
  row[f'count_frequency_{name}']=float(nodes.loc[pop,'count_frequency'].mean()) if pop.any() else np.nan
 return row,nodes
records=[];node_tables=[];event_rows=[];bounds=[];SELECTED={}
for rho in RATIOS:
 for name,mask in LAYOUTS.items():
  G=conductance(mask,rho);E=np.where(mask,3.,-3.)
  for phase_seed in PHASE_SEEDS:
   run_id=f'run_{len(records)+1:03d}';sol=integrate(INITIAL[phase_seed],G,E)
   stats,nodes=measure(sol,mask,G);records.append(dict(run_id=run_id,layout=name,rho=rho,phase_seed=phase_seed,**stats))
   nodes['run_id']=run_id;nodes['layout']=name;nodes['rho']=rho;nodes['phase_seed']=phase_seed;node_tables.append(nodes)
   for node,e in enumerate(sol.t_events):event_rows.extend(dict(run_id=run_id,node=node,time=float(t)) for t in e)
   z=sol.sol(np.linspace(0,END,2001)).reshape(N,3,-1)
   bounds.append(dict(run_id=run_id,min_v=float(z[:,0].min()),max_v=float(z[:,0].max()),min_s=float(z[:,2].min()),max_s=float(z[:,2].max())))
   if rho==1 and phase_seed==11 and name in ['patch','checker','random_301']:SELECTED[name]=sol
   (OUT/'progress.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(status='running',runs_completed=len(records),total_runs=24)))
   del sol
scan=pd.DataFrame(records);scan.to_csv(OUT/'layout_scan.csv',index=False)
node_metrics=pd.concat(node_tables,ignore_index=True);node_metrics.to_csv(OUT/'node_metrics.csv',index=False)
pd.DataFrame(event_rows).to_csv(OUT/'spike_events.csv',index=False)
bound_table=pd.DataFrame(bounds);bound_table.to_csv(OUT/'sampled_bounds.csv',index=False)

4. Compare individual initial-phase realizations¶

Each column displays a different observable, with common vertical scales across the two ratio cuts. Dots are individual runs at fixed layout; they are not confidence intervals. Nearby horizontal offsets distinguish the two phase seeds and have no physical meaning. No regression of synchrony on interface size is fitted to these six cases.

5. Inspect selected spatial states and source-sorted rasters¶

Use ratio 1 and phase seed 11, where all layouts have exactly the same G matrix. Snapshots use one common activation scale. Raster ranks place E sources first and I sources second; they are not spatial node indices. Differences in raster grouping across layouts therefore do not directly display spatial propagation. Snapshots and event order alone do not classify a traveling wave, spiral or stable attractor.

6. Separate global and within-type coherence¶

At ratio 1, compare global order with E- and I-population order for each initial realization. The source populations each have 18 nodes, versus 36 in the global measure. Group-size and supported-time differences still matter: large population order with lower global order may reflect a phase offset between coherent groups, rather than fragmented groups. Complete state synchronization is a separate question.

In [7]:

7. Validate spatial contracts and selected numerical accuracy¶

Check source counts, graph descriptors, exact equality of G across layouts at ratio 1, and the network-mean budget at both ratios. Translation equivariance permutes source types and initial states together, rather than treating translated copies as independent evidence. Validate sampled gates/reversal brackets and current signs.

For random_301, ratio 1, phase seed 11, compare independent DOP853/Radau trajectories over 0–200 and a tighter DOP853 run over 0–1000. Extend the patch, checkerboard and selected random run to time 2000 and compare windows 400–1000 and 1400–2000. These audits cover selected trajectories only and do not establish stationarity or all attractors.

Next extension and limits¶

Transfer the same E/I source rule to open boundaries and distance-weighted kernels, keeping source counts and strengths explicit. Compare fixed per-edge coefficients with a clearly defined normalization; the fixed-budget identity used here relies on regular out-degree. More phase seeds, random layouts, translations relative to initial fields and longer windows are needed before general placement claims or phase-boundary estimates.

This notebook uses one graph size, a 50/50 split, six specific layouts and two strength ratios. Its patch is one declared shape, not an optimum over clusters. Two phase realizations do not establish typical behavior, statistical significance or all basins. Spatial descriptors are mechanisms under comparison, not universal predictors. At ratio two, arrangement also changes local conductance totals; actual currents additionally depend on gates and recipient activation. Measured phase order does not establish wave type, chaos, stable attractors or biological balance. Numerical checks cover selected trajectories and stated horizons; measurement averages use a finite sampling grid without a separate grid-refinement study. No delays, noise, plasticity or physical-unit calibration are added.

Provenance: dynamics, gates and measurement definitions follow notebooks 11–13; periodic graph conventions follow notebook 09. Neuronal Dynamics §3.1 provides the reversal-current/first-order gate background, not the chosen spatial patterns or numerical parameters. SciPy solve_ivp documents integration and event handling. Logarithmic discrepancy plots use a display floor of 10⁻¹⁶.
